items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: It's a pleasure playing with him. These are people I had the pleasure of playing with

ctx.x: I'm thinking of musically as well as...

Harold Mabern. He's dedicated. It's a pleasure playing with him. These are people I had the pleasure of playing with, because of their sincerity and dedication to music, you know. You can tell. There's no falseness there and they want to make sure they do everything right at all times, you know. And let's see. J.J. Johnson, Max Roach. Miles Davis. He's dedicated.

items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: I think one time we played up there and Big Nick was the guest, and Joe Newman.

ctx.x: And Jillean gave us all these tapes. And so this is like —

Isn’t that something, the Rainbow Room. We were probably up there for maybe sometimes we’d be up there maybe three or four or five weeks at a time. And Duke Ellington would come by because Joe loved Duke, you know. Duke loved to sing with © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

the maestro and I’d tell him go ahead and play something, he’d play. Jimmy Jones would come by. Because Joe loved Jimmy Jones. And he’d always tell me, he would say, you know, not necessarily play like Jimmy Jones but listen. Which I had no problem with that because Jimmy Jones and Jerome Richardson were the ones that recommended me for the job with Joe Williams, you know. But yeah, isn’t that something. I think one time we played up there and Big Nick was the guest, and Joe Newman.
